findings.finding: Redaction-before-persist is described as a trust boundary but is NOT architecturally wired into the event-write path or asserted as a binding invariant. THREAT_MODEL §4 tags 'redaction happens BEFORE persist/embed/sync' as [proposed][mvp], the redaction ENGINE itself is [research]/OPEN (OQ-SEC-2, marked MVP-blocking but unresolved), and ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6 describes the `eventstore` module as 'append events + projections + outbox in one txn' with zero mention of a mandatory redaction step before INSERT. The redaction logic is parked in the `policy` module (§6: 'redaction rules'), which is NOT in the write path. So the single most-likely accidental breach (T-02 secrets-in-logs, rated Hi) has a control that exists only as prose, not as an enforced seam in the sole-writer transaction.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6 `eventstore` row ('append events + projections + outbox in one txn; FTS5; migrations') and `policy` row ('...redaction rules'); THREAT_MODEL.md §4 bullets tagged [proposed][mvp] and the §4 closing [open-q] 'What is the redaction detection engine?' [research]; OPEN_QUESTIONS.md OQ-SEC-2 status OPEN, MVP-blocking; DATA_MODEL.md §2.7 artifacts column `redaction_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unredacted'` (default state is UNREDACTED with no enforced gate that flips it before persist).
findings.proposed_fix: In ARCHITECTURE.md §15 (Security) and §6 (module decomposition), make redaction-before-persist a BINDING invariant with an enforced seam: the eventstore single-writer MUST route every event payload through a `Redactor` (owned by `policy`/`eventstore`) before the INSERT, and the write txn MUST set `redaction_status` to a non-default terminal value (redacted|summarized|quarantined) — an event row may never persist with `redaction_status='unredacted'`. Specify the MVP redaction engine concretely (curated high-recall token-prefix set ghp_/github_pat_/sk-/xox/AKIA/PEM/JWT + Shannon-entropy fallback on KEY=value lines, per THREAT_MODEL §4 open-q) and reference the §14 security test 'redaction-before-persist; secrets never in events' as the acceptance gate. Resolve OQ-SEC-2 to LOCKED before tasks-gen.

findings.finding: 'Secrets never in events/payloads' is asserted as an architecture-binding invariant (DRAFT §15) but there is NO enforcement mechanism and NO fail-closed check — it is pure convention. There is no schema constraint, no pre-INSERT validator, and no quarantine-on-detection path tied to EVENT_MODEL §23's required behavior ('Sensitive payload detected → Redact, downgrade sync/export eligibility, emit SensitiveOutputRedacted'). DATA_MODEL §2.1 events table has no integrity check tying secrets out; the only related events (SecretDetected/SensitiveOutputRedacted from EM §10.16) are not wired to any emitter in §6/§10. An invariant with no enforcement point and no test is untestable.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §15 ('Secrets only in the keychain; never in events/payloads') stated as [LOCKED] invariant with no mechanism; EVENT_MODEL_AND_AUDIT_TRAIL.md §23 failure-mode row 'Sensitive payload detected' and §10.16 events SecretDetected/SensitiveOutputRedacted — neither is mapped to an emitting component in DRAFT §6 modules or §10 background jobs; DATA_MODEL.md §3 source-of-truth matrix line 481 ('Secrets | OS keychain ... never in events/rows') is a claim, not a constraint.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §15: bind the redactor (above) to ALSO emit `SensitiveOutputRedacted` and, on a high-confidence secret hit in a payload that cannot be safely redacted, QUARANTINE the event (per EM §23) rather than persist it inline. Name the emitting component (the eventstore writer / policy redactor) in §6. Add an explicit §14 test: feed a payload containing each known token shape → assert no raw token reaches `payload_json` and a `SensitiveOutputRedacted` event is emitted. Make this the operational definition of the invariant so it is testable.

findings.finding: UDS peer-auth on macOS — the enforcement mechanism for trust boundary [b] (UI↔daemon) — is UNRESOLVED and partly wrong. DECISIONS ADR-004 and the draft cite `SO_PEERCRED`, which is a Linux-only sockopt and does not exist on macOS; the correct macOS path (`getpeereid()` / `getsockopt(LOCAL_PEERCRED)`) is only [proposed]/[research] (THREAT_MODEL §2[b], §7 spike #1). T-06 (local IPC snooping/spoofing, Med) and TR-13 depend on this check actually being implemented and correct. Because it is unconfirmed, the boundary is currently enforced ONLY by socket filesystem perms (0700 dir / 0600 node), which alone do not distinguish 'our UI' from any other same-uid process — and the draft itself concedes peer-uid is 'necessary but not sufficient' yet ships no capability token.
findings.evidence: DECISIONS.md ADR-004 ('OS-enforced peer auth via filesystem perms / SO_PEERCRED'); THREAT_MODEL.md §2[b] validation bullet ('Kernel peer auth via SO_PEERCRED (Linux-ism) / on macOS use getsockopt(LOCAL_PEERCRED) / getpeereid()' tagged [proposed]...[research]) and §7 spike #1 'Exact macOS peer-auth syscall ... confirm uid-equality is the right (and only) MVP check'; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6 `ipc` row ('versioned handshake ... peer auth') leaves the syscall unspecified.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §6 (`ipc`) and §15: LOCK the macOS peer-auth syscall to `getpeereid()` (with `LOCAL_PEERCRED` as the documented alternative), assert uid==daemon-uid as a hard reject-on-mismatch, and state socket-perms (0700 dir / 0600 node) as defense-in-depth NOT the primary control. Add a §14 IPC test: a same-uid process with the wrong/absent handshake is rejected. Note the single-user MVP-simplification explicitly (capability-token in handshake = [DEFERRED]) so the residual is recorded, not silently assumed.

findings.finding: PRD §13.4 REQUIRES the platform to detect and gate 'credential access' and 'secret file reads' and 'external network operations where policy requires approval' — but the agent boundary [d] leaves the default Gateway policy for an agent invoking git/gh/ssh/cat ~/.ssh directly under can_use_tool UNSET and explicitly punts it to 'the finalizer.' THREAT_MODEL §7 open-q #5 and §2[d] open-q both concede an agent can still try to invoke shell binaries (visible+gateable) but 'the policy default for shell tools needs to be conservative' — undefined. As drafted, the PRD §13.4 'secret file reads' / 'credential access' gating requirement is unmet and untestable for MVP because the policy that would enforce it does not exist.
findings.evidence: PRD.md §13.4 ('detect and gate dangerous commands, including: ... credential access; secret file reads; ... external network operations where policy requires approval'); THREAT_MODEL.md §2[d] open-q ('Should we deny the agent direct git/gh/ssh binaries on PATH ... Finalizer to set the default policy') and §7 open-q #5; ACTION_GATEWAY.md §12.3 gives examples (deny rm -rf /) but no rule covering reads of ~/.ssh/credential-helper output; EVENT_MODEL §10.16 has CredentialAccessAttempted/DangerousCommandDetected events but no emitter is wired in DRAFT §6.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §15 + §6 (`policy`/`gateway`): define a conservative default shell-tool policy: shell tool-calls matching credential/secret read patterns (~/.ssh, security find-generic-password, env dumps of token-shaped vars, cat of keychain-helper output) and network egress to non-allowlisted hosts are classified risk 3-4 and require explicit approval, emitting CredentialAccessAttempted/DangerousCommandDetected. Make 'dangerous-command detection' (which DRAFT §15 already leans on as the egress mitigation) a NAMED, testable component rather than an undefined hand-wave. Resolve THREAT_MODEL §7 #5.

findings.finding: The central security invariant the THREAT_MODEL explicitly asks the finalizer to assert as binding — 'there exists no code path by which an agent, the Brain, or the future phone mutates FS/git/external state except by a typed Action that passed policy + approval and produced an audit event' (THREAT_MODEL §3) — is NOT actually asserted as a binding, testable invariant in ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §15. §15 restates the pieces (chokepoint, no mutation outside Gateway) as descriptive notes but never names the negative invariant nor a test proving no bypass path exists. Without it stated as binding + tested, 'single mutation chokepoint' (§4.2 law #1) is an aspiration, not a verified property.
findings.evidence: THREAT_MODEL.md §3 ('Key invariant for the finalizer to assert as binding: there exists no code path by which an agent, the Brain, or (future) the phone mutates ... except by a typed Action ...'); ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §15 lists 'No mutation except via a typed, approved, audited Gateway action' as a bullet but §14 Gateway tests cover per-action behavior, not a no-bypass conformance assertion; §4.2 law #1 is stated without a verifying test.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §15: promote the THREAT_MODEL §3 sentence verbatim to a numbered BINDING invariant ('INV-SEC-1: no mutation path bypasses the Gateway'). Reference enforcement points: Claude can_use_tool, Codex host-routed approvals, Brain proposal-only seam, UI intents-only, fail-closed-on-audit-write. Add a §14 conformance test that every executor adapter is only reachable through the Gateway pipeline (no direct executor entrypoint) and that an event row exists for every mutation.

findings.finding: Untrusted Workflow Pack script gating is asserted (T-05, DRAFT §13) but the ENFORCEMENT is undefined and the residual is larger than acknowledged. WORKFLOW_PACKS §16.1 defines trust levels with 'untrusted' as the DEFAULT for locally-imported packs, and §21 non-goal forbids 'run arbitrary pack scripts without explicit trust and approval' — but (a) how trust is represented before signed packs is OPEN (OQ-WP-9, P1), (b) THREAT_MODEL T-05 concedes 'no sandbox for approved pack scripts in MVP,' and (c) DRAFT §6 `workflow` module only does detection/parsing/personalization-as-Gateway-actions and never states the gate that BLOCKS an untrusted pack's shell/hook/script from executing. The pack securityProfile/permissions model (WORKFLOW_PACKS §16.2) is not wired into the policy engine in the draft.
findings.evidence: WORKFLOW_PACKS.md §16.1 ('Untrusted ... Mutations require explicit approval'), §16.2 declared permissions, §16.3 'forbidden by default' (incl. 'Run network scripts without explicit approval', 'Install arbitrary binaries without explicit approval'); THREAT_MODEL.md T-05 residual ('no sandbox for approved pack scripts in MVP'); ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §6 `workflow` row and §13 Workflow Packs bullet (manifests read-only) — no enforcement of trust-level gating; OPEN_QUESTIONS.md OQ-WP-9 status OPEN, P1.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §13 + §15: state the binding gate — any pack command of type shell_command/hook OR any pack whose trustLevel != bundled_trusted must route every script/binary execution through the Gateway as risk>=3 with explicit per-action approval; the policy engine reads the pack securityProfile/permissions (WORKFLOW_PACKS §16.2) and DENIES forbidden-by-default ops (§16.3). Lock OQ-WP-9's MVP answer ('Unverified pack' badge + explicit consent + max friction). Record 'no script sandbox in MVP' as an explicit residual in §15.

findings.finding: Codex rollout 0644->0600 hardening has an unaddressed TOCTOU window. The plan is to chmod 0600 'on first read' (DECISIONS ADR-006, OQ-HARN-10), but Codex CREATES the rollout JSONL world-readable; between creation and the daemon's first-read hardening there is a window where another same-uid process/agent can read the transcript (which by definition contains secrets, asset A8). The draft never proposes pre-creating/owning the ~/.codex/sessions dir with restrictive perms (which THREAT_MODEL §4 lists as the stronger option 'or pre-create/own the dir') to close the window.
findings.evidence: DECISIONS.md ADR-006 ('rollout JSONL ... hardened to 0600 (bug #21660)'); OPEN_QUESTIONS.md OQ-HARN-10 ('Harden to 0600 on first read; startup self-check', MVP-blocking, status OPEN); THREAT_MODEL.md §4 Codex bullet ('daemon must chmod 0600 (or pre-create/own the dir)') — the dir-ownership option is mentioned but not chosen; RESEARCH.md line 78 (created 0644, issue #21660).
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §15: prefer the window-closing option — pre-create and own `~/.codex/sessions` (and the dated subdirs) with 0700 before launching Codex, so rollout files inherit a non-world-readable parent; keep first-read chmod 0600 as belt-and-suspenders. Add a §14 test asserting no rollout file is ever observable at 0644 by a second reader. Note the threat is intra-machine same-uid agent-to-agent transcript theft (relevant in multi-session MVP).

findings.finding: Execution-profile 'no silent account-hopping' (ToS-sensitive, DRAFT §15) is stated as policy but has no enforced technical control and the supporting question is unresolved. ACTION_GATEWAY §20.2 says 'Profiles cannot be silently switched by Project Brain' but the draft never states the gateway-level rule that REJECTS a profile change mid-session or a session.create that resolves to a different account than approved. OQ-INT-6 (usage limits without encouraging account-hopping) is OPEN/P1 with the answer being 'show usage transparency only; no auto-routing' — i.e., a UX choice, not an enforced invariant. T-12 is correctly flagged as a legal/policy (not code) question, but the binding behavioral guarantee (profile is fixed at approval time, changes re-trigger preview+risk) is missing.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §15 ('execution profiles explicit/auditable; no silent account-hopping — ToS-sensitive'); ACTION_GATEWAY.md §20.2 ('Profiles cannot be silently switched by Project Brain') — no gateway enforcement rule; THREAT_MODEL.md T-12 (open-q/policy); OPEN_QUESTIONS.md OQ-INT-6 status OPEN, P1; PRESEARCH.md line 151 ('Execution Profiles explicit/visible/auditable; no silent account-hopping').
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §15 + §6 (`gateway`/`policy`): make profile-binding a binding invariant — every session.create/team.start resolves an execution_profile_id at approval time, the resolved profile is recorded in the SessionStarted event, and any change requires a new approval (re-preview + re-risk per ACTION_GATEWAY §14.4 critical-field rule). Brain may never set/change a profile. Keep usage-transparency-only (no auto-routing) as the locked MVP answer to OQ-INT-6.

findings.finding: Agent egress isolation is correctly identified as the largest residual MVP risk and explicitly deferred — the stance is acceptable as an MVP-simplification — BUT the draft §15 overstates the compensating control. It claims the residual is 'mitigated by Gateway gating of mutations + dangerous-command detection.' Gateway gating does NOT mitigate exfiltration over the agent's own already-allowed model-API/network egress (T-01 residual is explicit about this), and 'dangerous-command detection' is itself an undefined/unbuilt component in the draft (see credential-gating finding). So the MVP residual is slightly larger than §15 implies.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §15 ('Largest residual MVP risk: no agent egress isolation ... mitigated by Gateway gating of mutations + dangerous-command detection, not eliminated'); THREAT_MODEL.md T-01 residual ('Agent can still exfil over its own allowed model-API/network egress (no egress firewall in MVP)') and §6 non-goal 'Egress firewalling of agents ... not built in MVP [deferred/research]'.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §15: keep egress isolation [DEFERRED] but correct the residual statement — Gateway gating bounds MUTATIONS, not data exfiltration over allowed egress; the only MVP reduction is keeping secrets out of agent-reachable surfaces (redaction + keychain-only). Cross-reference the (newly-named) dangerous-command/credential-read policy as the partial mitigation rather than implying a built egress control exists. Record the precise residual in the security non-goals list.

findings.finding: Brain 'redact before embed' (boundary [c], asset A9 — embeddings can memorize secrets) is tagged [proposed][mvp] in THREAT_MODEL §2[c]/§4 but is NOT reflected as an enforced seam in the draft. DRAFT §13 Brain seam and §6 `brainclient` describe feeding events/proposals but never state that content handed to the Brain for indexing passes the SAME redactor as the persist path. Since the Brain owns its own store the platform cannot retroactively scrub it, so an unredacted embed is a durable secondary leak the platform can't undo.
findings.evidence: THREAT_MODEL.md §2[c] mitigation ('Redact before embed — content handed to the Brain for indexing goes through the same redaction as persist' [proposed][mvp]) and §4 sink #2 ('embed -> before content reaches the Brain index'); ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT.md §13 Brain seam + §6 `brainclient` row — no embed-time redaction stated; DATA_MODEL.md §2.7 notes redaction summaries persist but not the embed path.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §13 + §15: state that the redactor is applied to ALL three sinks (persist, embed, sync) as a single shared component, and that any event/content emitted to the Brain over the outbox->MCP-notification adapter is redacted-by-construction (only redaction-safe projections/summaries cross the [c] boundary). Tie to PRD §11.x Brain action-boundary requirements and EM §15 (Brain consumes redacted projections).
